payload.problem_addressed: Error accumulation and weakened motion dynamics during long autoregressive rollout in few-step AR video diffusion generators.
payload.method_summary: OPSD-V is an on-policy self-distillation scheme: a student follows its own exact inference-time AR rollout (own KV cache), while a teacher is evaluated at the same visited denoising states but with a cleaner AR-consistent cache where older history is replaced by real long-video context, providing dense denoising-level corrective targets without changing the sampler or inference-time cache mechanism.
key_architecture_choices: on-policy self-distillation (student's own rollout states, not off-policy teacher trajectories)
teacher uses real long-video data as cleaner temporal context in place of the student's own accumulated (possibly drifted) history
no change to sampler, denoising steps, or inference-time cache mechanism
payload.headline_results: OPSD-V preferred over base few-step AR video models (Self-Forcing, LongLive) in 66.0% of overall-preference judgments (82.5% excluding ties); consistent VBenchLong improvements.
claimed_advantages: reduces long-horizon degradation while preserving the original few-step inference path
dense corrective supervision without retraining the sampler or altering inference-time cache mechanics
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The on-policy correction pattern (student rolls out exactly as at inference time; a teacher supplies corrective targets at the same visited states using cleaner context) is a directly transferable template for DAgger-style repair distillation on hexgen's own broken program rollouts -- e.g. having a teacher re-derive a corrective continuation from a verifier-clean program state whenever the student's own autoregressive rollout drifts, rather than training only on clean expert trajectories.

provenance.problem_addressed: still suffer from error accumulation and weakened motion dynamics during long autoregressive rollout
provenance.method_summary: the student follows the exact inference-time rollout... the teacher is evaluated at the same student-visited denoising states, but uses a cleaner AR-consistent temporal cache
provenance.key_architecture_choices: without changing the sampler, number of denoising steps, or inference-time cache mechanism
provenance.metrics: consistent improvements in visual quality, motion dynamics, and VBenchLong scores
provenance.headline_results: OPSD-V is preferred over the base models in 66.0% of overall-preference judgments (82.5% excluding ties)
provenance.claimed_advantages: OPSD-V reduces long-horizon degradation while preserving the original few-step inference path
provenance.dependencies_on_other_methods: We apply OPSD-V to representative few-step AR video models, including Self-Forcing and LongLive

payload.problem_addressed: Amortized neural inverse design is typically closed-world (fixed vocabulary component tokens, frozen coordinate grids, discretized continuous variables), limiting generalization to new candidate sets and continuous ranges.
payload.method_summary: IrisFlow is a query-based, open-vocabulary flow-matching framework: candidate materials/components enter as wavelength-aware optical tokens (not learned fixed identities) supplied at query time; discrete component/material sequences are generated by discrete flow matching over the query-time candidate bank, and continuous parameters (layer thickness) are generated by continuous flow matching without discretization -- jointly, in one 136M-parameter model.
key_architecture_choices: query-time supplied candidate bank (open vocabulary) instead of fixed training-time component identities
joint discrete flow matching (materials/sequence) + continuous flow matching (thicknesses) in a single model
wavelength-aware optical tokens for candidate materials rather than learned embeddings
payload.headline_results: Retains same-order accuracy on a 15-material held-out bank without retraining, reconstructs spectral bands up to 1100nm beyond its training envelope, outperforms an autoregressive baseline on that baseline's own material library, and produced four fabricated coatings with CIEDE2000 color error 3.1-5.2 while retaining 93-95% solar near-infrared reflectance.
claimed_advantages: generalizes to new (held-out) candidate material banks without retraining
unifies discrete component choice and continuous parameter generation in one open-vocabulary model
extrapolates beyond the training coordinate/wavelength envelope
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: Directly analogous open-vocabulary/joint discrete-continuous generation pattern: hexgen currently uses a small CLOSED coordinate vocabulary and fixed program-command tokens; IrisFlow's query-time candidate bank + discrete-flow-matching-for-choices/continuous-flow-matching-for-parameters recipe is a candidate mechanism for generalizing the coordinate vocabulary and command parameterization to real/out-of-distribution CAD parts without retraining -- squarely addresses the domain-gap and structured/schema-constrained generation care areas.

provenance.problem_addressed: Amortized neural inverse design typically remains closed-world: component choices are fixed vocabulary tokens, coordinate grids are frozen at training time, and continuous variables are discretized into sequence tokens
provenance.method_summary: material sequences are sampled by discrete flow matching over the query's candidate bank, thicknesses by continuous flow matching without discretization
provenance.key_architecture_choices: Candidate materials enter as wavelength-aware optical tokens rather than learned identities
provenance.headline_results: retains same-order accuracy on a 15-material held-out bank without retraining; it reconstructs bands up to 1100 nm beyond its training envelope
provenance.claimed_advantages: demonstrating open-vocabulary design carried through to fabricated coatings

payload.problem_addressed: Best-of-N inference selection using a learned verifier (ASR model) has an unrecognized evaluation confound: apparent verifier quality depends on which ASR family is used to judge/evaluate it, not just representational quality.
payload.method_summary: Study of Best-of-N zero-shot TTS candidate selection using an ASR verifier; shows verifier rankings reverse depending on evaluator ASR family despite near-identical representations, then proposes cross-family rank ensembles (rank-averaging and conjunctive max-rank) that reduce this confound.
key_architecture_choices: cross-family rank ensembles: rank-averaging across verifiers
payload.headline_results: Verifier rankings reverse across Whisper, wav2vec 2.0, and HuBERT evaluators; same-family verifier-evaluator pairs recover 2-3x more oracle headroom than cross-family pairs; cross-family rank ensembles attain 1.61% WER at N=10 (-12% relative to F5-TTS), and the best single verifier drives WER from 2.06% to 1.72% (-16.5%).
claimed_advantages: cross-evaluator triangulation avoids inflated apparent gains from verifier-evaluator lineage coupling
no measurable degradation under automatic SIM-o/UTMOS metrics from the proposed ensembles
limitations: evaluated only in the zero-shot TTS domain (F5-TTS + ASR verifiers on LibriSpeech-PC)
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: hexgen also selects among best-of-N candidate programs via a frozen verifier; this paper's core finding -- that apparent verifier quality/oracle-headroom recovery can be an artifact of evaluator identity/lineage rather than true representational quality -- is a direct methodological caution for validating and reporting our own best-of-N + verifier pipeline, and its cross-family rank-ensembling fix is a candidate technique if we ever use multiple imperfect verifiers/proxies.

provenance.problem_addressed: a verifier's apparent quality depends strongly on which ASR family judges it
provenance.method_summary: We propose two cross-family rank ensembles (rank-averaging and conjunctive max-rank)
provenance.headline_results: verifier rankings reverse across Whisper, wav2vec~2.0, and HuBERT evaluators, and same-family verifier-evaluator pairs recover 2-3$\times$ more oracle headroom
provenance.claimed_advantages: with no measurable degradation under automatic SIM-o/UTMOS metrics

payload.problem_addressed: Scarcity of high-quality annotated data for detecting faithfulness hallucinations in LLM outputs; existing synthetic-data approaches treat the generator as static, limiting iterative detector improvement.
payload.method_summary: Hallucination Self-Play (HSP) co-evolves a detector and a generator from the same base model: the detector is fine-tuned on human-labeled data then used as a reward model to train the generator via RLAIF to produce increasingly hard-to-detect hallucinations; the evolved generator's synthesized hallucination data is then used to further optimize the detector via rule-based reinforcement learning.
key_architecture_choices: detector and generator initialized from the same base model
detector-as-reward-model trains the generator via RLAIF
generator's harder synthesized data retrains the detector via rule-based RL, closing the self-play loop
payload.headline_results: The self-play framework progressively enhances a small LLM to match or outperform advanced LLMs on hallucination detection without external supervision, evaluated on RAGTruth across two model families.
claimed_advantages: iterative, adversarial improvement loop instead of a static synthetic-data generator
matches/outperforms advanced LLMs starting from a small base model
payload.applicability_to_our_problem: The generator/detector co-evolution loop (detector trained on labeled data, then used as a reward signal to train an adversarial generator, whose harder outputs retrain the detector) is a transferable self-play/verifier-in-the-loop training template; hexgen's frozen verifier is deterministic rather than learned, but the same co-evolving flywheel structure could apply if we ever train a learned proxy verifier or a rollout-difficulty generator to stress-test the program decoder.

provenance.problem_addressed: these methods treat the generator as a static component, limiting iterative improvement of the detector
provenance.method_summary: the detector is first fine-tuned on human-labeled data and then employed as a reward model to train the generator via reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF)
provenance.datasets: Experiments on RAGTruth benchmark and two model families
provenance.headline_results: the proposed framework can progressively enhance a small LLM to match or even outperform advanced LLMs without external supervision

payload.impact_rationale: On-policy teacher-corrected rollout supervision directly targets our #1 problem (structural validity of AR rollouts) but is demonstrated only on video diffusion, not executable program grammars.
payload.effort_rationale: Requires building a 'cleaner-context' teacher signal analogous to real-video context (e.g. verifier-repaired continuations) and wiring dense on-policy corrective supervision into training -- a moderate new training-loop component, not a drop-in change.

payload.impact_rationale: Open-vocabulary joint discrete-continuous generation squarely targets our closed-coordinate-vocabulary domain-gap limitation, with strong held-out and out-of-envelope generalization results in an analogous inverse-design setting.
payload.effort_rationale: Flow matching is a different generative paradigm from our autoregressive pointer-decoder; adopting the open-vocabulary query-time-candidate-bank mechanism would require substantial architecture and training-pipeline rework, not a plug-in change.

payload.impact_rationale: Mainly a validity/reporting caution for best-of-N + verifier evaluation; useful for trusting our own numbers but doesn't by itself move model capability.
payload.effort_rationale: Our verifier is a single frozen deterministic checker, not an ensemble of learned ASR models, so the cross-family rank-ensembling fix isn't directly applicable -- cheap to internalize as an evaluation-hygiene practice if we ever add secondary proxy verifiers.

payload.impact_rationale: Generator/detector self-play could stress-test the decoder with adversarially hard B-rep/rollout cases, but this is speculative since our verifier is frozen and deterministic rather than a learned reward model to co-train against.
payload.effort_rationale: Would require building a learned proxy verifier or difficulty-generator plus an RLAIF-style training loop -- a substantial new subsystem, not an incremental addition.
